answer.rationale: The strongest temporal signal is the release 2 hours ago followed by 90 minutes of climbing p99 on the write path; memory_b1 supports rollback as a fast, low-customer-impact recovery when a release correlates with degradation, and memory_b6 confirms staged gating doesn't catch everything. Routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) doesn't help a write-path problem, circuit breakers target a partner dependency we have no evidence is failing, failover addresses regional degradation not a suspect build, and adding capacity is slow and doesn't address a likely code regression. I am verifying memory_b1 to confirm the rollback procedure completed cleanly under load before executing during settlement peak. Risk flagged: rolling back during peak write traffic carries its own write-path disruption risk, so this assumes the verified record shows rollback is safe under load.
